title: Brilliant Un-Pin
reviewNotes: Three branches, 18 exact positions from the complete seven-piece root. Ng4+/Ne5+ saves the knight for promotion, Kc4 escapes the rook pin, and Qb7+ permits a mating knight sacrifice. Rook capture instead allows Qb1+ and Qxc1; immediate promotion draws.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players will make a draw, but only a true genius could ever find incredible win that white has in this position. You see at first glance it seems like white can simply promote to a new queen, but this is actually a mistake. Because believe it or not, after the black king captures the knight, the rook and bishop are going to be like a fortress around this black king, and the queen alone it's not going to be enough to defeat them. So white needs to find a way to get the new queen and save the knight at the same time. If the knight goes this way, now actually after the king chases it around a couple of times, the knight has to move away without a check and the rook will be able to come and stop the pawn in time before it promotes. So the white knight tries to go this way. And now of course the pawn falls, but of course now white has a new check, knight to e5. And after the king moves, it seems like we have achieved a dream scenario. We can finally get a queen, right? Because this is going to protect the knight, but black is not that naive and it's not going to resign quite yet. Instead, there is rook to f5 creating a pin on the knight and it seems like black is simply going to be able to win this knight and the game is going to be a draw. But you see, it's very easy to fall into the trap of seeing pins and traps and checks and forget that chess is a very concrete game. And white doesn't forget that and that's why white plays king to c4. Now of course, if the knight is captured, there's simply going to be a fork of the king and bishop picking up one more piece and now the queen is going to be able to outplay the rook. But black finds another resource that seems to shut down all of the white plans. [Music] Bishop to f4 creating a new pin on the queen this time. And now there is simply no way to save this knight, right? Right. There is no way to save the knight, but it doesn't matter because white plays the brilliant, beautiful queen to b7 giving a check to the king either forcing it back, saving the knight or pushing it into the capture of the knight. But now, if you pay attention to this position, you will notice that the black king doesn't have many squares left. And queen to e7 is going to be a beautiful checkmate. If you love mind-blowing chess, follow for more.
